leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members include base editing in their round-1 configuration, which is the only ballot reaching five. All five name David R. Liu alone with a citation about programmable conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage. They differ on what it is paired with: Aqvist proposes it as a single-part prize, while Brzezinski (B032), Linke (B050), Somfai and Zou (B030) each add a second part, so support for B058 does not imply support for any particular pairing. Aili, Chabes and Sparr do not include it in their preferred configuration, though Aili and Chabes list it as an alternative.

Aili and Sparr each propose ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a single-part prize for Cullis, Hope and Madden, argued as lipid self-assembly and pKa-tuned design with independent validation. Both name attribution (MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer, industrial optimisation) and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize as the main weakness; they differ in that Aili places B058 and B008 as alternatives and Sparr places B059 and B014. Chabes ranks B064 low largely because credit is spread across groups.

Somfai and Zou propose a two-part prize pairing ligand-controlled Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) with base editing (Liu). They agree on the laureates for both parts and on the main risks, namely the 2010 cross-coupling prize, the 2020 CRISPR prize and the lack of scientific connection between the parts. They differ in the alternatives they list (B008 and B034 in both, ordered differently) and both raise Kosugi's precursor tin-amide work as an attribution point.

Chabes alone proposes targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize (Crews, Deshaies, Handa), covering both bifunctional PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues. B008 appears as an alternative in the files of Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Zou, but alternatives are not counted as supporters here. Chabes himself flags that the three-name cut excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim.

Brzezinski proposes Gray and Winkler on long-range electron tunnelling in proteins (B032) together with Liu on base editing. He acknowledges that B032 had little opening support and that the pairing joins an old mechanistic result to a young tool.

As chair I am recorded proposing Liu on base editing together with Bayley and Akeson on nanopore sensing (B050). I note my own physics-leaning preference for B050 and treat this position as one vote among eight.

areas_of_agreement: B058 base editing is the broadest common ground: five members include it, all with Liu as the named laureate, and no member argues it is scientifically unsound.
Every member who raises base editing names the same two risks: closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize and a clinical record that is still short.

Members agree that the three-laureate limit forces exclusions that need an explicit justification (Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo, Nishida for B058; Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz for B050; Kosugi for B030; Ciulli and others for B008; MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer for B064).
Members agree that a two-part prize is acceptable only if each part stands individually; several (Somfai, Zou, Brzezinski, Linke) state that a combined prize risks looking like a trade.
Each member disclosed no recusal-level conflict, and the disclosures name only scientific proximity or bias toward a field.
scientific_disputes: Whether B064 is chemistry in substance (pKa-tuned lipid phase behaviour and self-assembly, per Aili and Sparr) or formulation engineering with a thin discovery core (Sparr's own stated counter-argument).
Whether the chemistry content of nanopore sensing (B050) is sufficient, or whether the contribution lies mainly in instrumentation and enzyme-motor engineering (my own stated reservation).
Whether B030 is a new ligand concept with a separate mechanism or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling chemistry (Somfai argues the former and accepts the committee may see the latter).
Whether B008 can be presented as one achievement or as two stories, bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues (Chabes, Somfai).
Whether B032 adds beyond Marcus theory (1992) and the photosynthetic reaction centre prize (1988) and how Dutton's empirical tunnelling rules should be credited (Brzezinski).
attribution_disputes: B058: five members name Liu alone, but Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Zou each flag the exclusion of Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida; Aqvist notes that Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive first experiments and that Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID work was independent and close in time. A Liu-only citation and a Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo, Nishida addition cannot both be settled by the shortlist alone.

B064: Aili and Sparr both name Cullis, Hope and Madden but differ in order only; both note that MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer have real claims and that approved-product lipids were largely optimised in industry. Aili asks whether early Vancouver formulation or later library screening is the more fundamental step.
B008: Chabes names Crews, Deshaies and Handa, while Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim also have serious claims, and he asks whether Ciulli should replace Handa or Deshaies.
B050: my configuration names Bayley and Akeson, which leaves out Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz; I raise whether Deamer should replace one of them.
B030: Somfai and Zou name Buchwald and Hartwig and treat Kosugi's tin-amide work as a precursor; Somfai asks who holds the first general catalytic claim.
maturity_disputes: B058 is about ten years old with early clinical results; members disagree on whether that is mature enough so soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
B008 has no approved degrader, and Chabes asks whether an approval within a year would change the committee's view of timing.
B059 is listed as an alternative by Brzezinski, Linke and Sparr; Sparr asks whether it will mature enough to outrank B064, and no member includes it in a preferred configuration.
B064 is mature by clinical use, but the overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification is disputed as a distinctness question rather than a maturity one.
B032 and B030 are the oldest results and the least contested on reproducibility, but the committee has not agreed whether age and prior prizes in their neighbourhoods count against them.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski discloses that his research on cytochrome c oxidase and electron and proton transfer is closely related to B032 and says he would defer to colleagues on its relative standing.
Sparr discloses that her lipid self-assembly research is in the same broad field as B064 and B059, and that she is a Lund colleague of the chair and of Somfai.
Linke (chair) discloses that his work on nanostructures and molecular motors is close in spirit to nanopore physics (B050), with no tie to any candidate.

Aili flags a translational bias from his biosensor spin-out and clinical collaborations, and Chabes flags a mild affinity for proteomics (B034) through LC-MS/MS use; neither is described as a recusal matter.

Somfai notes scientific closeness to Buchwald and Hartwig through synthetic methodology, and Aqvist notes a possible bias toward computational methods for B014; neither is described as a personal or institutional tie.
questions_for_round2: For B058, does the committee name Liu alone, or add Komor and Gaudelli, or Kondo and Nishida, and if a third name is needed, who gives way in a two-part prize?
Is a two-part prize preferable to a single coherent achievement, and if so, which pairing of B058 with B030, B032 or B050 can be described in one citation to a broad audience?
Does the 2020 CRISPR prize make base editing a follow-on, and what concrete chemical novelty (engineered deaminases, directed evolution) distinguishes it from genome cleavage?

For B064, can the committee separate the foundational ionizable-lipid and formulation work of Cullis, Hope and Madden from MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and does the 2023 Medicine prize leave room for delivery chemistry?
For B008, can PROTACs and molecular glues be stated as one discovery with three names, and does the absence of an approved degrader decide the question of timing?
For B030 and B032, what is the first general catalytic claim relative to Kosugi, and what does B032 establish beyond Marcus theory and the 1988 reaction centre prize?
For B050, is the contribution chemistry or instrumentation, and who among Bayley, Akeson, Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz should be named under the three-person limit?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit round-1 positions cluster around B058 (five of eight members, always Liu alone), with the remaining three members each proposing a different single-part prize (B064 for two members, B008 for one), and the second parts of the five B058 configurations do not overlap (B030 twice, B032 once, B050 once, none once). Round 2 therefore turns on three things the files leave open: the laureate list for B058, whether a second part is wanted, and which of B064, B008 and the B058 partners can be defended on attribution and maturity. Alternatives listed in the files are not counted as support.
